entities.name: Preop statin RP outcomes
observations: In a prospective-database cohort of 3,042 radical prostatectomy patients, statin use at surgery was not significantly associated with biochemical recurrence (adjusted HR 1.06, 95% CI 0.86–1.31) over median 70 months.
Among 1,256 patients with biopsy Gleason 3+3=6, preoperative statin use was not significantly associated with upgrading (adjusted OR 0.78, 95% CI 0.58–1.04).
Observational exposure reported at surgery may be misclassified; residual confounding remains possible.

entities.name: Statins and RP recurrence mixed
observations: Preoperative statin-BCR evidence is inconsistent: SEARCH reported adjusted HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.50–0.97), whereas NYU reported HR 1.15 (95% CI 0.82–1.61); pooled estimate was HR 1.00 (95% CI 0.80–1.19).
Other cohorts report null preoperative associations; some favorable studies have uncertain exposure windows or retrospective confounding.
